title: YOU WERE NEVER SUPPOSED TO LOVE ANYTHING MORE THAN HIM
paragraphs:
YOU WERE NEVER SUPPOSED TO LOVE ANYTHING MORE THAN HIM
Why Jesus Is the First Love We All Need — And the Only One That Will Never Break Us
There’s a kind of silence that only shows up after everything you thought would fulfill you… doesn’t.

It’s the quiet after the messages stop.
After the excitement fades.
After the relationship you prayed for becomes the reason you cry at night.
After success finally arrives… and somehow still feels empty.
That silence isn’t just loneliness.
It’s a question.
And deep down, you already know what it’s asking.
“Why isn’t this enough?”
Because somewhere along the way, you were taught to build your life on things that were never designed to carry your soul.

You gave your first love to people who couldn’t stay, to achievements that couldn’t hold you, to approval that kept moving the goalpost. You poured yourself out, hoping something—anything—would finally pour back into you.
But nothing ever did.
Not completely.
Not permanently.
And that’s because your heart wasn’t created for “something.”
It was created for Someone.

In Revelation 2:4, Jesus speaks words that cut through time and land directly in this generation:
“ἀλλὰ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην σου τὴν πρώτην ἀφῆκες”
“But I have this against you, that you have abandoned the love you had at first.”
That word “ἀγάπην” (agapēn) is not shallow affection. It is covenant love. Sacred devotion. A love that consumes identity, direction, purpose.

And Jesus is saying—
You didn’t just drift.
You replaced Me.
Sit with that.
Because this isn’t just theology.
This is personal.
You didn’t wake up one day and decide to walk away from your first love. It happened slowly… subtly… quietly.

You started needing validation more than you needed His voice.
You started chasing outcomes more than you chased His presence.
You started loving what He gives… more than loving Him.
And maybe no one noticed.
But heaven did.
Because the greatest tragedy isn’t sin.
It’s misplacement.
It’s loving temporary things with eternal intensity.
And still wondering why your soul feels unstable.
Jesus didn’t come just to fix your behavior.
He came to reclaim your heart.

In Matthew 22:37, He says:
“ἀγαπήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου…”
“You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart…”
Not part of it.
Not what’s left over.
All of it.
Because whatever gets your first love… gets your life.
And here’s the truth most people don’t want to face:
Whatever you love first… you obey most.

That’s why you keep going back to things you know are hurting you.
That’s why you struggle to let go of people God already told you to release.
That’s why your faith feels inconsistent.
It’s not because you don’t believe.
It’s because something else has your first love.
And Jesus is not competing for a place in your life.
He is calling you back to the place where everything finally makes sense.
Back to the beginning.
Back to Him.

Because before there was heartbreak…
Before there was insecurity…
Before there was striving…
There was a God who already chose you.

In Jeremiah 31:3, written in Hebrew, God says:
“אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם אֲהַבְתִּיךְ”
“I have loved you with an everlasting love…”

Not a temporary love.
Not a conditional love.
Not a love that depends on your performance.
Everlasting.

Before you failed.
Before you wandered.
Before you gave your heart to things that couldn’t protect it.
He already loved you.

So when Jesus calls you back to your first love…
He’s not asking you to lose something.
He’s inviting you to come home.
And maybe that’s what this moment is.
Not coincidence.
Not just another post you scrolled past.
But a divine interruption.
Because deep down, you know something isn’t aligned.

You feel it when you’re alone.
You feel it when the noise fades.
You feel it when your soul starts asking questions your distractions can’t answer.
This is that moment.
The moment where you stop pretending you’re okay.
The moment where you stop calling emptiness “normal.”
The moment where you finally admit—
“I’ve been loving the wrong things first.”
And if that’s you…
Don’t numb it.
Don’t ignore it.
Lean into it.
Because conviction is not condemnation.
It’s an invitation.
Jesus is not exposing you to shame you.
He’s calling you back because He still wants you.
Even now.
Even after everything.
Even after the things you don’t talk about.
Especially those things.
So be honest.
Let this not just be something you read.
Let it be something you respond to.
Because your response matters.
And someone else needs to see it too.
Stay close to truth.
Stay close to Jesus.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—not just emotionally, but spiritually—there is something waiting for you.
Because supporting this isn’t just about content.
It’s about souls.
It’s about truth.
It’s about making sure someone, somewhere, doesn’t feel alone in their struggle.

If you’ve been fed here…
If God spoke to you through this…
Then don’t stay silent.
Support what is feeding your spirit.
Not because you have to.
But because you want to be part of something that brings people back to Jesus.
Because at the end of the day…
Nothing you put first will ever love you back like He does.
Nothing.

Not success.
Not relationships.
Not approval.
Not even your own strength.
Only Him.
Only Jesus.
And until He becomes your first love again…
Everything else will keep falling apart in your hands.
Because some emptiness isn’t meant to be fixed.
It’s meant to lead you back.
